_comment: Voice contract: docs/design/character-profiles.md 'Grand Lift Attendant' (precise/kind; rule first, then the human way through it; kindness arrives as practical information). Forge-tier post, so the base hub is already the post-permit read -- see pallass_forge_smith.json's note.

hub.speaker: Lift Attendant
hub.text: The cage runs on the counterweight cycle. Down at the quarter bell, up at the half. You have four minutes, and I'll say so again at three.

text_variants.text: Down at the quarter bell, up at the half. The Liscor news rode up on the same cycle as the tin did. I heard it four times before the cage reached the landing.

options.text: [Ask what the tier made of the seal news.]

options._comment: v0.16 P2 start. requires-hidden on read_the_lift_manifest (banked only by lift_manifest_slate, which near_pallass never interacts), so the 3-row pin and index navigation are untouched.
options.text: Your manifest says one crate of tin, three cycles held.

cycle.speaker: Lift Attendant
cycle.text: Once a quarter, for inspection, and the notice goes up two days ahead so nobody is stranded. If the day catches you up here anyway, the service stair at the west end stays open. Nine flights. Honest work, and open.

traffic.speaker: Lift Attendant
traffic.text: Smiths down at the quarter bell, clerks up at the half, and one crate of tin that has been late three cycles running. I know this tier by what it carries. You I haven't placed yet, {addr}. Came up on a stamp, then. Stamps don't show on my schedule.

options.text: Not yet placed. I'll take that.

seal.speaker: Lift Attendant
seal.text: It came up the shaft the way everything does, one voice at a time, each louder than the last. Liscor settled what was under its stone. The tier will talk about it for a week and then it will talk about tin again. The tin is four cycles late, {addr}. Liscor is two hundred miles away.

options.text: That's fairer than most of what I've heard.

ledger_pitch.speaker: Lift Attendant
ledger_pitch.text: Four cycles, and it will be five. The permit office holds the queue and the office's own supplies are in it, so the office cannot clear the queue until the queue clears the office. Nobody may skip it. That includes the queue.

ledger_brief.speaker: Lift Attendant
ledger_brief.text: Walk the offices in order, {addr}, and get it in writing. Start at the quarter bell or you will spend the day at windows. Read the forms properly, if you read forms. Or put the crate on the cart yourself and carry it down, which is not how it is done. The consignee is a den shop on the market tier.

ledger_brief_two.speaker: Lift Attendant
ledger_brief_two.text: The stamp clerk on the market tier holds the entry side. The permit window holds the release side. The consignee signs last. She cannot sign first. Down at the quarter bell.

ledger_report.speaker: Lift Attendant
ledger_report.text: Say it plainly. I have a cage to run in three minutes and I would like to run it happy.

options.text: [The offices countersigned each other. It's released.]
[The exemption was in the forms the whole time.]
[I carried it down myself. It's on her dock.]

ledger_settled.speaker: Lift Attendant
ledger_settled.text: Then the manifest is clean and the cage runs happy. Down at the quarter bell.

text_variants.text: You carried it. Two tiers, on your own back, for a family that does not know your name. I have run this cage eleven years and watched a great many correct people wait. Ride free while I am on the gate, {addr}. That is the only thing I own to give.
You made the offices sign each other's paper. I am going to tell that story at every quarter bell for a month. The crate goes down on the next cycle, on top of the load.
It was in the forms. Four cycles, and it was in the forms. Do not speak to me until the half bell.
